report:
## Research Findings

The evidence does not support the view that this claim is false—multiple independent lines of research consistently show an inverse association between olive oil consumption and stroke risk.

**Randomized controlled trial evidence (strongest design):** The landmark PREDIMED trial randomized over 7,000 high-cardiovascular-risk participants in Spain to a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil, one with nuts, or a low-fat control diet. It found the olive oil-supplemented diet significantly reduced incidence of stroke, myocardial infarction, and cardiovascular death (https://www.urmc.rochester.edu/MediaLibraries/URMCMedia/neurology/documents/PREDIMED.pdf).

**Meta-analysis of observational and intervention studies:** A meta-analysis combining case-control, cohort, and intervention studies (including ~38,673 participants for stroke outcomes) found olive oil consumption inversely associated with stroke risk (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24775425/).

**Large prospective cohort study:** A study of over 7,000 French adults aged 65+ (Bordeaux/INSERM) found olive oil users had lower stroke risk; a secondary analysis using blood oleic acid levels (a biomarker for olive oil intake) found those with the highest levels had a 73% lower stroke risk (https://timesofmalta.com/article/Olive-oil-could-lower-stroke-risk-study-finds.371508).

**Mortality data supporting the mechanism:** JAMA Internal Medicine cohort analyses (Guasch-Ferré et al., 2022) found higher olive oil intake associated with lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, consistent with a protective cardiovascular effect (https://www.michelegargiulo.com/blog/why-olive-oil-could-be-the-real-secret-to-longevity).

**Conclusion:** The claim is well-supported, not false. Evidence spans an RCT, meta-analyses, and cohort studies with biomarker confirmation. Caveats: effects appear specific to replacing saturated fats/butter, and much of the benefit may reflect the broader Mediterranean dietary pattern rather than olive oil in isolation. Still, the specific claim that more olive oil reduces stroke risk is supported by good-quality evidence.
